newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs seen starting New Year with hangover.
newsitem.headline: OLOs seen starting New Year with hangover.

text.p: Belgian linear bond (OLO) yields are seen rising in the New Year -- the hangover from 1996's year-long party.
But dealers said on Monday that the correction was likely to prove short-lived as cash generated from profit-taking was quickly reinvested.
"Everyone is afraid of what is going to happen at the beginning of the year," a trader at a large domestic bank said.
"But I'm convinced that even if people are willing to sell...cash has to be reinvested so in the end it will prove a non-event and the market will return to where it is now."
At the beginning of 1996 OLOs rallied as investors built up heavy positions, with the yield on benchmark 10-year bonds falling to around 6.40 from 6.70 percent.

There was a large correction at the end of January as a large domestic player adjusted its positions, pushing the yield back up to 6.90 percent. But from around February/March the market began what turned out to be a slow and steady climb.

In early trade on Monday the yield was at 5.86 percent, with the spread over Bunds at 10 basis points, compared with around 70 at the start of the year. A dealer at another domestic bank saw the yield falling to 5.50 percent by March 1997.
"Some people may be tempted to take their capital gains. (1996) was such a good year for the banks...but what will they do with the money? They can't put it in repos," he said.
"Personally I think signs of an economic pick-up are exaggerated and the repo will stay at 3.00 percent or lower, so I think 5.50 percent is possible in Belgium by the beginning of March," he added.
Another trader also expected the buy trend to re-assert itself. "We can continue for six to nine months until short rates begin to move up again," he said.
